newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch receiver fails to sell Shipmair Rotterdam.
newsitem.headline: Dutch receiver fails to sell Shipmair Rotterdam.

text.p: Attempts to sell dry cargo charterer Shipmair Rotterdam B.V. as a going concern have been unsuccessful, official receiver John Wolfs told Reuters Friday.
Shipmair, which specialised in the agribulk trade between Europe and Latin America, went bankrupt on May 23 with debts totalling $3.7 million.
Wolfs said attempts to sell the Rotterdam-based firm had failed but its investments in Latin American companies Shidobra and Flutrans may still be sold successfully.
He said he is aiming to sell the interests by July 1. "Several bidders have come forward. There are Latin American companies amongst them," he said.
A bankruptcy judge is reviewing the bids and will give his verdict next week, added Wolfs.

Brazilian company Shidobra, which is wholly-owned by Shipmair, owns a 40 percent stake in Flutrans, a company formed to develop the harbour of Antonina in Brazil. It has invested 10-15m guilders in the port.
Brazilian interests own another 40 percent of Flutrans with the remaining 20 percent held by IBHS, International Bulk Handling Services N.V.
